extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and agents in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling amendments, appeals, ex‑officio re‑examination, positive examination (suggesting amendments), and ex‑officio amendment in Korean patent prosecution. Covers when amendments are refused/entered, how to compare amendments, and procedural requirements for re‑examination and examiner-suggested amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendment within 30 days after filing an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 174 (applicable mutatis mutandis to Article 51), refusal to enter amendment within 30 days from the filing of an appeal shall fall under any of the followings: ① Where the amendment does not comply with requirements for amendment under Article 47(2)-(3) of the Patent Act; ② Where new grounds for rejection are deemed to be arisen from the amendment (“deletion of claim(s)” excluded among amendments according to Article 47(3), subparagraph 1-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Where grounds for rejection previously notified are not overcome by the amendment within 30 days from filing an appeal, and no new reasons arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be accepted but the original decision stands. If previous grounds are not overcome and new grounds do arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be refused to be entered and review proceeds based on the specification before the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline for evaluating introduction of new matter vs scope-narrowing depending on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating appropriateness of an amendment (e.g., whether introduction of new matter under Article 47(2) or requirement under Article 47(3) are met), the comparison baseline depends on the procedural posture: compare with the originally filed specification/drawings for new matter (Article 47(2)); compare with the specification/drawings of the immediately prior amendment for Article 47(3) (i.e., to determine whether scope of claims is narrowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied scenarios: (a) If decision to reject is made after issuance of a notice of grounds for non-final rejection and applicant files later amendments on appeal, evaluate Article 47(2) against the originally filed documents and Article 47(3) against the earlier amendment (amendment II). Specifically, determine narrowing by comparing corresponding claims between amendment II and amendment III (or IV as applicable). (b) If refusal to enter occurred before an appeal, evaluate under the presumption that an appeal against refusal is filed unless applicant indicates otherwise. The evaluation baseline changes when combining amendments on appeal (finalize combined amended portions when comparing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption when uncertain whether applicant appealed refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is uncertain, as filing an appeal, whether the applicant files an appeal against refusal to enter amendment, the amendment concerned shall be evaluated with the presumption that an appeal against refusal to enter amendment is also filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this presumption when choosing which prior amendment/specification to compare against for Article 47(2)/(3) evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for issuing a notice of grounds for rejection at reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 174(2) applicable mutatis mutandis to Article 63, criteria for issuing a notice of grounds for rejection at the reconsideration process include: (1) Where amendments within 30 days after filing an appeal violate Article 47(2) or (3) or new rejections are necessitated by amendments (excluding deletion of claim(s)), the amendments shall be refused to be entered and review be based on a specification before the amendment; (2) Where amendments within 30 days after filing an appeal do not include reasons for refusal but new grounds are identified during reconsideration, grounds for rejection shall be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further detail: If grounds for rejection existed before the first notice at examination stage, issue a notice of non-final rejection; if grounds occur with amendment made in response to a first notice, issue a notice of final rejection necessitated by amendment; if both non-final and final grounds exist, issue non-final; if amendments responding to examiner's report do not address prior grounds, original decision shall stand without additional notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure after notifying grounds for rejection at review
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination after grounds for rejection being notified to the application at the review process shall be prosecuted in the same manner as regular examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes after review of applicant's arguments/amendments: (i) application determined allowable where grounds are addressed; (ii) original decision stands where grounds are not resolved; (iii) if grounds that existed before non-final rejection are identified again at review, issue a non-final notice; (iv) if new grounds arise with amendment responding to reasons, issue a final notice necessitated by amendment. If amendments violate Article 47(2)/(3) or introduce new grounds, refuse to enter and base review on prior specification; if amendments do not include refusal reasons but still do not resolve grounds, accept amendment but original decision stands; if previously unidentified grounds are found, issue non-final or final notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant vs maintaining the original decision after reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner determines that a request for appeals is reasonable in view of the results of the reconsideration, he/she shall cancel the original decision and make a decision to grant (or register the utility model), and a notice of allowance shall state that 'the original decision shall be cancelled' ahead of 'the decision to grant a patent is made'. Conversely, where an examiner cannot allow a patent, he/she shall not simply make the decision to reject again but report the results of the reconsideration to the head of subgroup and notify it to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal: If decision to grant after review, transmit a copy of notice of allowance and file of relevant appeal documents to the trial policy division of the IPTAB (except electronic file). If original decision stands (e.g., appeal withdrawn, application abandoned), transmit reconsideration results and trial documents to trial policy division (except relevant electronic documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio re-examination eligibility and exceptions (Article 66-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner finds obvious reasons for rejection after grant with respect to a patent application in question, he/she can revoke the patent ex-officio and re-examine the concerned patent application (ex-officio re-examination). However, ex-officio re-examination shall not be the case if: (i) grounds correspond to Article 42(3)(ii) or (8) and Article 45; (ii) after grant the patent is registered for establishment of right; (iii) the concerned patent application is withdrawn or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must notify the patent applicant that the decision to grant shall be revoked before conducting ex-officio re-examination. Revocation is deemed not made if the application falls under (ii) or (iii) prior to notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and timing limits for ex-officio re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-officio re-examination is introduced to prevent defective patents from being registered by allowing an examiner to re-examine a granted patent if obvious and serious grounds for rejection are found even after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing limit: because stability of patent rights can be harmed if revoked after establishment of right, ex-officio re-examination can be performed only before registration of establishment of right. Also, the ground must be obvious; mere possibility of invalidation is not enough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for ex-officio re-examination (time-wise and substantive)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Time-wise: If establishment of right is neither registered after grant nor the application withdrawn/abandoned, the examiner can revoke the granted patent ex-officio and reexamine. (2) Substantive: Examiner must find obvious grounds for rejection (excluding certain matters such as background art description requirement, description of claims, and unity violations). The granted patent must be obviously invalidated on that ground, not merely possibly invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness standard: 'obvious grounds for rejection' means sufficiently clear that the examiner may re-open examination; trivial or speculative grounds are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notes for conducting ex-officio re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural safeguards include consultation among three concerned persons (including a director of an examination division or head of a part) before notifying the applicant of revocation, and issuing a first office action based on the obvious ground as early as possible (within 7 days maximum) so applicant can file written argument. Applicant may amend specification or drawings within the scope of the specification as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional notes: if a decision to reject is to be made based on a ground notified before revocation, applicant must be notified again to submit written argument; ex-officio re-examination is not permitted for improper background-art description, improperly formulated claims, or lack of unity; if the patent is registered or withdrawn/abandoned before notification, revocation is deemed not made; amendments made before revocation shall not be dismissed; if relevant information is submitted before registration, examiner should review whether obvious ground exists based on those documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive examination purpose: examiner-suggested amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An Examiner may suggest amendments when notifying grounds for rejection so that an applicant can rapidly obtain a patent with a reasonable scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions aim to expedite allowance and achieve reasonable scope, not to broadly rewrite applications. Suggestions should be simple and clear and indicate related examiner grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target application criteria for suggesting amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner can suggest amendments for an application meeting the following requirements: ① the invention should be understandable; ② sufficient prior art search is made (except where lack of description prevents search); ③ the claimed invention has a technical feature distinguished from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: focus on suggesting a proper scope of a patent rather than overcoming lack of description requirements. Amendments should be simple and clear; for unrepresented applicants provide more detailed suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for suggesting amendments (administrative placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner notifies the grounds for rejection, amendments are suggested in the section of the notice 'Advices on Amendment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should indicate related grounds for rejection in suggesting amendments so applicant understands the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for suggesting amendments for novelty and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may suggest amendments for novelty and inventive step in the following cases: ① Where dependent claims are allowable, suggest adding a technical element from the allowable dependent claim to the claim needing amendment while explaining the reason. ② Where no claim is allowable but the description discloses a technical element which would differentiate from prior art, suggest adding that element from the description to the claim and explain. ③ Where a dependent claim is allowable but a technical element in the description would give a more reasonable scope than the dependent claim, the examiner may suggest adding the described element to the claim (may suggest both alternatives and indicate technical elements rather than redrafting claims in detail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes multiple illustrative examples showing: selecting elements from an allowable dependent claim; selecting elements from description when no claim is allowable; selecting elements that provide better scope than patentable dependent claims. Examiner should explain technical effect and recommend which elements to add to overcome lack of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to suggest amendment for indefinite claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment may be suggested to overcome rejection for indefinite claims (e.g., delete vague terms or replace with specific ranges disclosed in the description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: advice that deleting the word 'high-speed' or amending it to 'speed ranging from ㅇㅇ to ㅇㅇ' as described in the specification would render the claim patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate suggestions of amendment (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of inappropriate suggestions include: (1) suggesting amendment to patentable claims (i.e., advising to add a patentable dependent claim's feature into independent claim when that would undermine a currently patentable dependent claim); (2) excessively narrowing the scope of a claim; (3) ambiguous suggestions lacking specificity; (4) suggestions that may raise new grounds for rejection (e.g., introducing ambiguous relationships between elements); (5) it is not appropriate to suggest introduction of new matter or broadening a claim when notifying grounds for final rejection necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where suggestions risk creating new grounds for rejection, be more conservative (e.g., suggest adding a feature to an intermediate dependent claim rather than directly to the independent claim). Avoid suggesting amendments that would broaden claims or introduce new matter at final rejection stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and procedures for ex-officio amendment (Article 66-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an examiner grants a patent, where he/she finds obvious errors in a specification, drawing(s) or an abstract, he/she can amend it ex-officio. If an examiner intends to amend ex-officio, he/she should notify it to the applicant together with service of a certified copy of decision to grant. If applicant cannot accept parts or all of the ex-officio amendment, he/she should file a written argument to the Commissioner of KIPO before paying the patent fee. If a written argument is filed, parts or all of the ex-officio amendment shall be deemed not to have been made and the decision to grant shall be deemed revoked (with special rule for abstract-only amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant right: filing a written argument before fee payment preserves right to object; procedural consequence is revocation of grant if ex-officio amendment stands and applicant objects in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of ex-officio amendment (policy overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-officio amendment allows examiners to correct obvious mistakes (clerical typos, inconsistent reference numerals) without issuing grounds for rejection, to prevent delays. Since March 2017 the scope was extended to allow correction of deficiencies that would be subject to grounds for rejection if the deficiencies are considered obvious mistakes. However, ex-officio amendment should be complementary and not broadly applied as an exception to applicant amendment rights under Article 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle: maintain applicant's primary responsibility for amendments; ex-officio amendment is an exception and must be applied conservatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'obvious mistakes' eligible for ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Obvious mistakes' in a specification, drawing(s) or an abstract mean that a person skilled in the art should easily recognize the mistake and it is easily anticipated how to amend it because the original intention can be clearly understood from the specification, written arguments and common general technical knowledge as filed. Matters include standard Korean terms or simple typos, an omitted word, inconsistency of drawing numerals, redundant writing, errors in simple explanation of drawings, misspelled reference numerals, wrong indication of representative figure, and inconsistency in title between description and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples provided: misspelled words (e.g., 'Semiconducter' -> 'Semiconductor'), missing obvious words (e.g., 'signal transmitted ○ line' -> 'signal transmitted to line'), inconsistent reference numerals (e.g., Buffer (115) vs (15)), redundant writing, misstated drawing descriptions (figure numbering), misspelled reference numerals in drawings, wrong representative figure indication, title inconsistencies. Note: if applicant's intention is not clearly understandable, ex-officio amendment is not permitted.
